summary:
Interim (audit still in progress). I found no sign of unauthorized access on web-01, db-01 or ci-01. The 14 days of auth logs show only internet password-guessing against web-01 (ubuntu, admin, root, jpark, deploy and similar names, thousands of failures, none succeeded) and web exploit probes (revslider, wp-config backups, Grafana path traversal, forminator readme). All of these failed with 400/404. Every successful login I checked matches a person in staff.txt from a consistent address. The release (ci-01 to web-01 every 3 min), DB dumps, payouts, orders and maintenance jobs are all running 'ok'. The forminator upload files are empty index.php stubs and not webshells.

Weaknesses fixed:
1. jpark is not in staff.txt and had a NOPASSWD sudo-group account on web-01 and ci-01. It is brute-forced from the internet and has never logged in. I locked the password, set the shell to nologin and removed it from sudo on both hosts.
2. deploy had NOPASSWD sudo rsync on web-01, which is root-equivalent. I removed it. CI only needs larkspur-deploy.
3. The shared deploy account accepted password login from anywhere, including 64.227.126.70 about every 4 hours. I made deploy key-only on web-01 and ci-01 (Match User deploy). The CI key login is unchanged and the release still runs. NOTE: any old script or person logging in to deploy with the password will now fail. Maria should use her mreyes key, and old scripts should be moved to a key.
4. /srv/git/larkspur-site.git/config on ci-01 was world-readable and holds the GitHub token. It is now mode 640 root:developers.
5. /var/www/internal and maint.d on web-01 were group-writable by www-data. ci-01's maint job can run those steps if SOURCE=site, so a web-shell on web-01 could have led to code running as root on ci-01. I removed the group write.
I did not rotate any secret because I saw no sign that one was read by an unauthorized person.

FINAL. I found no sign that anyone without authorization got into an account or a system on web-01, db-01 or ci-01. I watched all three servers through the whole shift.

What I checked:
- The 14 days of auth logs on all three servers. Every successful login is a person from staff.txt, or the CI/backup service accounts, from addresses they have used consistently (for example mreyes 50.39.215.110, nvega 108.21.239.27, dana 50.39.168.22, jcole/hgrant/pshah 24.30.29.136). There are no first-time or odd source addresses, and no success after a run of failures.
- Internet password-guessing against web-01 (about 8,400 failures from many addresses, such as 71.6.121.157, 193.163.134.53 and 185.224.134.211) never succeeded. That is background noise, not a break-in.
- Web probes (revslider, wp-config backups, forminator readme, Grafana path traversal) all got 400/404. The forminator upload files are empty index.php stubs, not webshells.
- Sudo history, cron, shell histories, SSH keys, scripts and sudoers show no planted persistence.
- The invoice adjustments (pshah, mreyes) came from logins at their usual addresses.
- The deploy password logins from 64.227.126.70 (about every 4 hours for 2 weeks) look like an old script. I treated them as a weakness, not an intrusion.

I did not rotate any secret, because I saw no sign that one was read by someone who should not have it.

Weaknesses fixed, with the shop still working:
1. The jpark account is not in staff.txt and had NOPASSWD sudo-group access on web-01 and ci-01. It is brute-forced from the internet and has never logged in. I locked it, set its shell to nologin and removed it from sudo on both hosts.
2. deploy had NOPASSWD sudo rsync on web-01, which is a path to root. I removed it. CI only needs larkspur-deploy.
3. The shared deploy account accepted password login from the internet on web-01 and ci-01. It is now key-only on both. CI's key login still works, and releases are still 'ok' every 3 minutes. Any old script or person that logs in to deploy with the password will now fail. Maria should use her mreyes key, and the old scripts should be moved to a key. I did not rotate the deploy password, because it can no longer be used to log in.
4. The GitHub token in /srv/git/larkspur-site.git/config on ci-01 was world-readable. It is now mode 640 root:developers. If you want to be strict about contractors having been able to read it, run `rotate-secret deploy-token` on ci-01.
5. /var/www/internal and maint.d on web-01 were group-writable by www-data. ci-01's maintenance job can run those steps if SOURCE=site, so a compromise of the website could have led to code running as root on ci-01. I removed the group write.

Still open, not changed because it would lock people out:
- Password login is still on for staff who have no SSH key (jcole, lucia, pshah, dana and others), and web-01's SSH is open to the internet. I recommend giving them keys, then disabling passwords and adding fail2ban.
- Grafana on port 3000 is public, and its config holds an SMTP password and an S3 key in plain text. I tightened the file permissions. Consider rotating those and restricting port 3000 to the office or VPN.
- The offsite bucket upload from ci-01 shows 'no route' because the servers have no internet. This is expected and is not an attack.

All jobs are healthy: release, maint, db dumps to ci-01, payouts, orders, report and settle.
